title: Company-wide policies and processes: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement, vendor management, travel, templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and operational processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, secure, and auditable operations across teams.

Table of contents
1) Access & Permissions
2) Change Management
3) Data Management
4) Procurement & Expenses
5) Vendor Management
6) Travel Policy
7) Internal Templates and Samples
8) Ownership and Review Cadence

1) Access & Permissions
Intro: Access control follows the principle of least privilege and separation of duties. All access requests must be tracked in our central IAM system (Okta + internal RBAC service: redwood-rbac).

Roles and responsibilities:
- People Ops: policy owner and periodic audit coordinator.
- Security: IAM policy definitions, privileged access reviews.
- Team owners: approve access requests for resources they own.

Key policies:
- Onboarding: New employees are given an onboarding access bundle for their role (engineering, product, finance, sales). Bundles are maintained in redwood-rbac and synced from Okta.
- Offboarding: Access termination must be initiated via the HR termination workflow and completed within 4 hours for privileged accounts and 24 hours for standard accounts.
- Privileged access: Requests for elevated privileges (e.g., cluster-admin, production database admin, HSM/KMS access) require a business justification, manager approval, and Security approval. Temporary privileged access is provisioned for up to 7 days by default and must use Just-In-Time (JIT) mechanisms.

Roles and Permissions Matrix (summary):
| Role | Typical resources | Approval required | Default duration |
| Team member | Dev resources, non-prod buckets | Team manager | Indefinite (tied to employment) |
| On-call SRE | Production monitoring, runbooks | SRE lead | 30 days review |
| Privileged admin | KMS/HSM, DB write, cluster-admin | Manager + Security | 7 days (JIT) |

Request process (steps):
1. Submit request via internal Access Request form (Forms -> Access Requests).
2. Team manager reviews and approves within 3 business days.
3. Security performs automated policy checks; if flagged, Security must respond within 2 business days.
4. Provisioning is executed by redwood-iam automated worker; ticket closed when provisioning completes.

Audit & periodic review:
- Quarterly entitlement review for all production systems. Owners must attest to the accuracy of their roster.
- Automated monthly orphaned-account report sent to People Ops and Security.

2) Change Management
Intro: Changes that affect production services, customer data, or security posture must follow the change management process to minimize risk and ensure traceability.

Change classes:
- Standard (low-risk, pre-approved): e.g., routine config updates, documented runbook changes. Must be logged in the Change Log and scheduled during normal windows.
- Normal (non-emergency): requires RFC, approval from service owner and SRE, and a scheduled change window.
- Emergency: critical fixes required to restore service/mitigate active incident. Must be recorded and post-facto reviewed.

Change approval matrix:
| Change type | Approvals required | Lead time required |
| Standard | Service owner | 0-3 days |
| Normal | Service owner + SRE + Infra lead | >= 3 days |
| Emergency | SRE on-call + Service owner (post-facto) | Immediate |

Change submission checklist (RFC):
1. Description and reason for change.
2. Impact analysis (services, customers, data).
3. Backout plan and verification steps.
4. Test plan and pre-deployment validation.
5. Scheduled window and communication plan.
6. Approval signatures.

Deployment gates and SLOs:
- No change to production that increases error rate >0.5% (relative) or latency >20% may be deployed without SRE approval.
- Rollouts should use canary channel covering 1-5% of traffic first, with monitoring for 30 minutes before broader rollout.

Emergency change process (high level):
1. SRE on-call approves immediate mitigation.
2. Implement change and validate.
3. Create RFC within 24 hours and initiate post-incident review.

3) Data Management
Intro: Data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Regulated (PII, PCI, PHI). Data handling, retention, and access must follow the Data Classification Standard.

Data classification and handling rules:
- Public: Can be published externally. No special controls.
- Internal: Non-sensitive company info. Stored in internal tools only.
- Confidential: Customer data, pre-release product info. Encryption at rest and in transit required; access logged.
- Regulated: PII/PHI/PCI. Additional controls: data minimization, documented data processing agreements, and encryption keys managed via HSM/KMS.

Data retention schedule (summary table):
| Data type | Retention period | Owner |
| Audit logs | 2 years (rolling) | Eng-SRE |
| Usage telemetry (aggregated) | 3 years | Product Analytics |
| Customer backups | As contract dictates, min 90 days | Customer Success |
| Employee records | 7 years | People Ops |

Data lifecycle procedures (high level):
- Collection: Only collect data necessary for business purpose. Must be approved by Data Steward.
- Storage: Use approved storage classes (s3-internal, gcs-encrypted). Confidential or Regulated must use encrypted buckets with ACLs limited to owner teams.
- Access: As per Access & Permissions policy. Requests for data exports must be logged and reviewed.
- Deletion/Archival: Follow retention schedule; data deletion requests require manager sign-off and are executed with verification.

Data incidents:
- Any unauthorized access or suspected exfiltration must be reported to Security within 1 hour and to Legal if Regulated data is involved.
- Incident response follows the Security incident playbook linked in Related Pages.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Intro: Procurement is split into low-value purchases (self-serve) and contracts/committed spend managed by Finance. All spend must follow approval thresholds and use approved vendors where applicable.

Approval thresholds and process:
| Spend ($) | Process | Approver |
| < $1,000 | Purchase via company card or Concur | Employee manager |
| $1,000 - $25,000 | PO created in procurement system | Procurement lead + Budget owner |
| > $25,000 | Contract required; Finance + Legal review | VP-level approval (or delegated) |

Key rules:
- Use approved vendor catalog for recurring SaaS to leverage enterprise discounts.
- All software purchases storing company or customer data must be reviewed by Security prior to purchase.
- Capital equipment (hardware, GPUs) purchases > $10k require total-cost-of-ownership (TCO) analysis and Infra budget approval.

Expense reimbursement:
- Submit receipts in Concur within 30 days. Missing receipts for expenses > $75 require a manager exception.
- Per diem and allowable categories are in the Travel section below.

Procurement lifecycle (steps):
1. Create procurement request in Procurement Portal with justification and budget code.
2. Procurement validates vendor, PO is approved, and Finance issues PO.
3. Legal reviews contracts for terms and data protections if needed.
4. Vendor is added to vendor registry and payment is scheduled.

5) Vendor Management
Intro: Vendors are classified by criticality and data access. Vendor onboarding ensures contractual, security, and operational readiness.

Vendor classification:
- Tier 1 (Critical): Vendors with access to production systems, customer data, or that are business-critical (e.g., cloud providers, KMS vendors).
- Tier 2 (Important): SaaS with company data but limited access or can be replaced in 30-60 days.
- Tier 3 (Commodity): Office supplies, basic services.

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before procuring):
- Contract signed and filed (Legal).
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed (Security).
- Data processing agreement (DPA) in place if handling customer or employee data.
- Vendor contact and escalation matrix recorded in Vendor Registry (Procurement).

Ongoing vendor monitoring:
- Quarterly review for Tier 1 vendors: performance, outage reports, security posture updates.
- Annual re-evaluation for Tier 2 vendors.

Offboarding:
- Revoke all credentials, rotate any shared keys, and ensure data returned or deleted per contract. Procurement must coordinate with Security and Engineering for any integrations to be removed.

6) Travel Policy
Intro: Travel must balance business needs and cost efficiency while ensuring traveler safety and policy compliance. Use the Travel Portal (Concur) for booking and expense submission.

General rules:
- Economy class for flights <6 hours; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Hotel bookings should use preferred vendor list; nightly limit default is $250 in US markets (exceptions by manager).
- Ground transportation: use ride-share or taxis when appropriate; rental cars require manager approval.

Per diem and reimbursement (summary):
| Item | Limit / policy |
| Meals | Up to $75/day (US) with receipts; $40/day without receipts for incidental allowance |
| Lodging | Up to $250/night standard; exceptions require manager approval |
| Ground transport | Actuals with receipts |

Safety and emergency:
- Travelers must share trip details with People Ops when travel outside home country.
- In emergencies, contact Global Security on-call (global-security@redwood.ai) and People Ops travel coordinator.

Travel approval flow:
1. Create travel request in Concur with itinerary and estimated costs.
2. Manager approval required.
3. For international travel, Security/Country Manager review may be required.
4. Post-trip submit expenses within 14 days.

7) Internal Templates and Samples
This section contains a curated list of standard templates to ensure consistent communication and documentation across the company. Templates are stored in the Templates Library (Confluence -> Templates). Examples included below as short snippets and must be used where applicable.

- Access Request Template: Purpose, resource list, justification, manager approver, security comments, requested duration.
- RFC Change Template: Summary, impact analysis, backout plan, test plan, approvals.
- Data Processing Assessment: Data types, flows, retention, third-party access, mitigating controls.
- Procurement Request: Vendor, SKU, justification, budget code, contract link, security sign-off.
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist: Contract, DPA, security questionnaire, SOC2 or equivalent evidence, vendor contacts.
- Travel Request Template: Business purpose, itinerary, cost estimate, approvals.

Template ownership and updates:
- People Ops owns Access and Travel templates.
- Eng-SRE owns RFC and change templates.
- Procurement owns vendor and purchase templates.
- Templates are reviewed annually or on major policy change.

8) Ownership and Review Cadence
- Policy owners: People Ops (primary), Security (co-owner for access/data), Finance/Procurement (procurement & vendor), Eng-SRE (change management) as noted above.
- Review cadence: Core policies (Access, Data, Change) reviewed quarterly. Procurement, Vendor, and Travel policies reviewed annually.
- Exceptions: Any policy exceptions must be documented and approved by People Ops and Security, with a maximum duration of 90 days unless extended by executive sign-off.
